findings.title: Routing/controller param mismatch in add_members and remove_member
findings.body: Both `add_members` and `remove_member` use `params.require(:group_id).to_i` to look up the group, but the routes declare `delete "members"` and `put "members"` at the top level of `resources :groups` (not inside a `collection do` block), so Rails generates member routes `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id/members` with the group id under `params[:id]`, not `:group_id`. Every real request from the frontend (which calls `Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)`) will hit `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param not found: group_id` and return 400, making add/remove of members non-functional in production. The controller should use `params[:id]` (as the sibling `update` action does), or the routes should be wrapped in `collection do` and the group id passed in the body. The spec suite passes only because it injects `group_id:` directly into the params, bypassing the real routing.

findings.title: Stray inside {{#each}} loop
findings.body:
The template introduces ` ` inside the `{{#each m in members}}` block (line 19) with no matching opening `
`. This was added by this PR (visible as a `+` line in the diff). It will produce malformed HTML on the public group members page and may disrupt the surrounding table layout/browser rendering. The closing tag should be removed.

findings.title: Specs bypass real routing and hide the add_members/remove_member param bug
findings.body: Both `add_members` and `remove_member` specs pass `group_id:` directly in the request params (`xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: group.id, ...` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, ...`). Because controller specs populate them straight into `params`, the tests succeed even though no route actually maps `:group_id` from the URL. They also exercise HTTP methods that partly disagree with the routes (e.g. the "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example uses `:put` against the `remove_member` action whose only declared route is DELETE). The suite should drive the actions through the real `/admin/groups/:id/members` URLs and methods so the routing/param mismatch in `groups_controller.rb` is caught.

findings.title: Usernames are not trimmed before lookup
findings.body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` splits the comma-separated string without stripping surrounding whitespace, so a payload like `"alice, bob"` produces `" bob"` and `User.find_by_username(" bob")` will not match the existing user `bob`. Either strip each element (`username.strip`) or rely on a username lookup that normalizes whitespace; otherwise users typed with accidental spaces silently fail to be added.

findings.title: findMembers has no error handler and may silently drop pagination races
findings.body: `findMembers` returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` chain but never attaches a rejection callback, so a failed request (e.g. network error, 404, 500) is swallowed and the promise resolves to `undefined`. Callers like the `next`/`previous` admin actions and `setupController` of `group-members` invoke `return group.findMembers()` and get nothing useful on failure. In addition, two concurrent calls (e.g. rapid clicks on next) both write `user_count`/`offset`/`members` on the same record, so an earlier response can clobber a later one. Adding a `.catch` (or at least surfacing the error) and guarding against overlapping requests would make pagination reliable.
